name: EOSBet
rootCause: The game contract does not check the transfer action must initiated by eosio.token or token contract of the game itself.

descriptions.text: The game contract does not check the transfer action must initiated by eosio.token or token contract of the game itself.
the attacker exchanged true EOS token with fake token within the vulnerability in the code, winning without betting.
The law of the random number generated by DEOSBET was cracked by hackers.

On 12 September 2018, EOSBet on EOS was exploited through a smart contract bug that allowed unauthorized withdrawals, resulting in an estimated loss of $200,000 (about 40,000 EOS). The contract failed to enforce input validation and assertion checks, enabling attackers to mint or extract tokens beyond legitimate deposits. A flawed transfer function in EOSBet’s contract allowed external calls without proper input validation or assertion checks, enabling attackers to bypass authorization and illegitimately mint or withdraw tokens. This led to an 'infinite mint' vulnerability.
